name: com.themethodic/candor
title: Candor UI docs
description: Candor UI docs and component suggestions. Read-only, no key, never serves paid source.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search Candor UI's components, hooks, blocks and patterns by what they do ("approve a tool call", "cost estimate", "session list"). Returns names, tiers and one-line descriptions; read one with get_component_docs.

query.description: What you're looking for, in words.

tier.description: Only items this tier unlocks: free, pro (free and Pro) or premium (everything).

tools.name: get_component_docs
tools.description: Read one item's docs as Markdown: what it is, its tier and install command, an example with the import paths an app uses, every prop, function, type, and the LocaleProvider string keys.

version.description: A release, e.g. "6.1.0", the version the project has installed. Default: the version the server's URL passes (`?kit=`, which `npx candor-ui mcp` writes from candor-lock.json). Candor UI serves only the current release's docs, so for any other version the answer is the current page with a note saying so.

tools.name: suggest_components
tools.description: Describe the screen or feature you're building; get the Candor UI items that fit, why, the matching patterns and screens, and an install command per tier. When nothing in Candor fits, it says so rather than suggesting something close. Pass `sdk` so only your agent SDK's adapter is suggested. Read each suggestion's docs before using it.

task.description: What you're building, e.g. "a chat where the agent asks before deploying".

tier.description: Only suggest what this tier unlocks. Leave it out to see everything, with tiers marked.

sdk.description: The agent SDK the app uses: ai-sdk (the Vercel AI SDK), claude (the Claude Agent SDK) or ag-ui. Only that SDK's adapter and block versions are suggested. Leave it out and no adapter is installed; the answer says which to add.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List every item by group (Chat, Agent work, App shell, …; the app scaffolding groups, Layout, Charts, Team, Billing and Admin, after the agent groups), or one group's items with descriptions.

group.description: A group's title, e.g. "Chat" or "Full-stack blocks". Leave it out for the overview.

tools.name: get_pattern
tools.description: Read a pattern as Markdown: a common problem in agent UIs (approvals, traces, cost guards, …) and the components that solve it.

slug.description: The pattern's slug, as search_docs or suggest_components gives it.

version.description: A release, e.g. "6.1.0", the version the project has installed. Default: the version the server's URL passes (`?kit=`, which `npx candor-ui mcp` writes from candor-lock.json). Candor UI serves only the current release's docs, so for any other version the answer is the current page with a note saying so.

tools.name: list_screens
tools.description: List the screen catalogue by area (talking to the agent, approving and controlling, watching the work, …), one line per screen: what it's for and its slug. Read one with get_screen.

area.description: An area's title, e.g. "Watching the work". Leave it out for every screen.

tools.name: get_screen

slug.description: The screen's slug, as list_screens or suggest_components gives it, e.g. "approvals-inbox".

version.description: A release, e.g. "6.1.0", the version the project has installed. Default: the version the server's URL passes (`?kit=`, which `npx candor-ui mcp` writes from candor-lock.json). Candor UI serves only the current release's docs, so for any other version the answer is the current page with a note saying so.

From the candor-agent-ui skill; works with or without Candor.

tools.name: theme_check
tools.description: Check a brand file (candor-brand.css, or any CSS that sets Candor's tokens) the way `npx candor-ui theme check` does: colour contrast of every text and edge pairing in light, dark and high contrast, each with its ratio and the ratio it needs, for the base and then for each brand scope ([data-brand="<name>"], as the theme builder writes several brands in one file) as a theme of its own, labelled (Light in [data-brand="acme"]) and counted in the totals; then the --cd-motion-* and --cd-sound-* values against the motion manifest; then token names and data-slot selectors against the token manifest, as warnings that don't fail the check (a --cd-* name the kit doesn't read, with the nearest one it does; a value outside a token's range; a --cd-show-* or --cd-draw-* value the Pro motion-drawings item has no drawing for, as motion-value, with the values it takes; an internal --cd-* name a brand file shouldn't set; a [data-slot] selector no component renders). Call it with the file's contents after you edit candor-brand.css, and fix what it reports before you say the theme is done. Returns a short summary (failures first, with a suggested lightness that would pass; findings with file, line and the fix), then the findings as JSON (ok, motionChecked, counts, themes with every pairing and, for a brand scope's, its brand, suggestions, motionAndSound.findings, tokens.findings). Anything it can't read (a color-mix(), a var(), a sound file) is reported as not measured, never as a pass. Sound files are not measured here: the server can't see your public/ folder, so `npx candor-ui theme check` in the project does that. It checks against the current kit; an older @candor-kit in the file is checked against the current names, with a note. It reads only the CSS you send, follows no @import and fetches nothing. At most 256 KB. Example arguments: { "css": ":root { --primary: oklch(0.55 0.2 260); --cd-motion-pop-dur: 140ms; }", "filename": "candor-brand.css" }

css.description: The CSS to check: the whole text of candor-brand.css (at most 256 KB).

filename.description: What to call it in findings (default candor-brand.css).
